cut_corridor.alt_text: Two eight-by-eight grid boards side by side, the same board one instant apart. In (a) object B stands as a circle on R5C2, the only entrance to a dead-end corridor, and a dotted route runs from object D through that cell and up the corridor to D's target at R1C2. In (b) B's owner has declared done: B is now a square on a walled cell, the dotted route is gone, and the shaded region D can still move in no longer contains its target.

panel_state.shape: seal on the corridor entrance, target inside the corridor

cut_twocut.alt_text: Two eight-by-eight grid boards side by side, the same board one instant apart. Object D at centre must reach R8C7, and a wall block leaves two routes round it: a northern one through R4C6 and a southern one through R7C6. In (a) E is already a frozen square on the southern cell and that route is drawn in long grey dashes, while the northern route is dotted and open through B. In (b) B has declared done, is drawn as a frozen square, and the shaded region D can move in no longer contains its target.

method.hand_placed_elements: none; every cell, route and count is computed
method.minimum_vertex_cut: exhaustive search over free cells up to size 3
method.reachability: breadth-first search over free cells, with walls and the objects of players that have declared done treated as blocked and all other objects passable
method.replay: accepted moves parsed from interactions.json and applied to instance.json start positions; no state is taken from scores.json
method.routes: breadth-first shortest paths under the same blocking rule

population.scope: cycle losses in 3p and 6p, Qwen3.8 and DeepSeek-V4.1

rendering.colour_is_redundant: object mobility is shape, a frozen cell is cross-hatched, lost cells are hatched, the reachable region is outlined, and the two routes use different dash patterns
rendering.page_width_note: the document's \textwidth, 455.24411 pt, so \thesisfig scales the figure 1:1
rendering.palette_audit: house palette; VICTIM vs ACTOR 9.85 and VICTIM vs MUTED 0.06 CIE L*, both below the 10.0 grayscale screening heuristic, which is why no meaning rests on hue alone
